thread:
maria: FYI i spotted a quota-attribution anomaly at ~16:02 UTC. lots of requests counted twice when proxied via auth-proxy. looks correlated with claim TTL vs cache TTL mismatch.
jon: can you drop the log lines? is this project keys or ephemeral SA tokens?
tariq: mostly ephemeral SA. quick grep showed `auth_proxy: claim_expiry=1700000000 token_ttl=30s cache_ttl=60s` so cache outlives token and stale claims get reused -> extra attribution.
alex: suggestion: add `claim_checksum` label to request metrics and show an origin_heatmap split by `token_type`. also add a simple `claim_stale_rewrites` counter.
maria: good. jon, can you add the label to the histogram and ship a 1% canary in auth-proxy?
jon: plan: (1) add label + promql tweak, (2) deploy auth-proxy/canary w/ 1% traffic, (3) enable `claim_stale_rewrites` counter behind flag, (4) collect 1 hour of samples.
tariq: use this promql to catch mismatches: ```sum by (claim_checksum, token_type) (increase(api_requests_total{handler=\"proxy\"}[5m])) / sum by (claim_checksum, token_type) (increase(token_issued_total[5m]))``` should highlight claims where requests > issued tokens.
alex: on console UX, add a short diagnostic blurb to the quota dashboard: "If requests > issued tokens for a claim, check auth-proxy claim TTL mismatch" with a runbook link.
maria: rollout gating: require canary <0.1% errors and no P50 regression. if `claim_stale_rewrites > 0`, keep canary and bump sampling to 10% for that origin.
jon: opening PR now. adding flag `auth.proxy.claim_labeling=true` and sampling config in the PR body.
deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-proxy/canary -> k8s-redwood/us-east-1 (id: deploy-2026-05-12-009) :rocket:
tariq: i'll run the promql against staging and drop screenshots in ~1h. if mismatch >2x we'll rollback the canary.
maria: thanks all. after we validate i'll add the heatmap to the quota dashboard and a one-paragraph runbook note. :thumbsup:
